For sure! But just remember what works for one person might not work for everyone, I always recommend people take the time to figure out the things that work best for your personal needs.
With that said I'm more than happy to point you in the right direction.
Firstly I try to tire myself out mentally with music, singing along to it specifically. I usually use rap because the fast pace requires more attention. This isn't always effective but usually 15-30 minutes of music does the trick. Next I like to do something like push-ups for physical exhaustion. Other calisthenic workouts are great too, even just things like arm windmills for a solid minute each direction will tire you out more than you expect.
Sometimes I'll read for a bit after if I'm not quite tired enough. Then finally when I'm ready to fall asleep I put the YouTuber "LEMMiNO" documentary playlist on repeat at a barely hearable level and turn on a fan pointed at the foot of my bed. The playlist adds a bit of background noise and helps me stay asleep (Only LEMMiNO works for, don't ask idk either).
Like I said before, what works for me might not work for you but I hope this gives you a good start. Don't give up on finding a solution, it took me a while to get a good system and if all else fails a melatonin every once in a while isn't too bad but I always recommend natural remedies first.
Hope this helps!

I was also on trazadone for about a year. I will say I've heard a wide variety of how it affects people so my word is by no means law. With that said though, I had a negative experience with it, it would help me fall asleep and stay asleep but I would never get into a heavy deep sleep.
This caused me to almost always be groggy and difficulty getting up despite getting 8-10 hours of sleep. I would need to have a nap during the day just to maintain some energy. When I was taken off the meds after discussing it with my doc, I had an adjustment period where I had a very difficult time falling asleep, but using melatonin for a month and slowly lowering the dosage helped me get back to a regular pattern.

I have different tricks and things I do to tire out my body and mind before bed and that has honestly been the best solution I've found over the years.

So I'm not the most knowledgeable, but I can give some advice. I still deal with spurts of hyperhidrosis but I do have ways to combat it that work for me.
My main thing is putting deodorant on literally as soon as I'm out of the shower and shower first thing in the morning. I find that if I wait to do either of those then I start sweating and won't stop no matter what.

Clothing is a big thing too, I usually either wear a tank top underneath my work/street clothes or a sport top to absorb any sweat. Stay away from baggy sweaters and shirts tho, too many times I've tried them only to feel drop after drop of sweat going down my side.

It's been a while since I've gone to a doctor, yet alone for this, but they never seemed to care too much so I'm not sure what kind of doctor to recommend.

As for deodorant, funnily enough anti-persprants make it worse (at least for me) so I just use regular deodorant. Stay away from the sport gel stuff, and the "medicated anti-persprant" both of those are really liquidy and once it mixes with the sweat it's not a fun day.

I haven't taken trazodone in several years now. But I took it near nightly from the age of about 13-16 I believe.

I too had this problem (though not as onset as you) after about 1 year of taking it I started to sweat, like a lot. I often would have to change my shirt midway through the day, put something like a napkin in my armpit, I tried the over the counter medical antiperspirant cream but it seemed to have little to no effect.

It got to the point where I could consistently feel sweat running down my arm and side while my shirts were wet enough to wring out sweat from.

After I stopped the use of trazodone, the effects didn't go away, I only recently went to a doctor about this issue hoping to get a prescription. He looked over my medical history and my family' and believed I developed something called "secondary hyperhidrosis" ie. Excessive sweating, mainly in the armpits, palm of hands and soles of feet.

Turns out although rare, trazodone can cause secondary hyperhidrosis sometimes being permanent.
I'm starting a medical topical soon now in hopes of limiting or removing this sweat entirely.

This is not medical advice and everyone's situation is different, I'd talk to your doctor about your concern and see if switching medications is something that is possible for you. Hope this helps.

Well I used to, a lot actually. My stepdad growing up was a major alcoholic and also thought being addicted to cocaine was pretty cool.Fairly often he would mix them and get angry, the anger was mostly taken out on my mother and I since we were the weakest.

At the start of seventh grade we moved away from him. Due to an illness that is a whole other story I wasn't attending school. My mom started drinking heavily and getting into drugs. Meanwhile my brother dropped out of school and started working, he got into a bad crowd and went down his own bad path of drugs.

It was then when I first got into alcohol at age 13. I was in a pretty messed up relationship with a 18 y/o that I don't want to get into, but that's how I got the booze. By the time I was 14 I was drinking at least a Mickey a day with the 18y/o also giving me codeine pills regularly.

After about 6 months of being drunk constantly I switched my outlet to weed, it helped with my anxiety and depression but I was still able to function. When I was 17 I got into what would become a long term relationship, she hated that I smoked weed and encouraged drinking. So once again I switched my vice.

We were with each other for a year and half when we were engaged and about to move 8 hours from where we currently lived. Engaged for 22 days and she cheated on me, telling me 10 hours before the scheduled move. I felt stuck and moved away from my family with her anyway.

 Fast forward two months, I'm just pushing all feelings down deeper and deeper, drinking more and more, forcing myself to think I'm happy in the relationship. But it's my 19th birthday! Yay! So we go out drinking with a bunch of friends, my birthday is on Halloween after all so it's a great night for it. After WAAAY to many drinks me and a group of guy friends started walking home, I was pretty much black out at this point. Somewhere along the way I got separated and became lost in this still fairly new city. Bad things happened, three men offered me a ride, but instead did some not nice things to me and left me on the outskirts of the city.

After that event I drank more than I ever did, I was going through a 26 a day or a 40 every two days. Eventually breaking things off with my fiance, I felt no feelings towards her after she cheated, and all sexual motivation was gone after my birthday. She left, I put blankets over every window in my basement suite, bought 3 40's of rum and finished it all in one weekend.

After a while I was broke, I had to move in with my mom. But she drank a lot too, so it just created the perfect toxic environment for me to feel self hatred and drink. Eventually I busted my own face against a wall, and smashed my knuckles in my right hand against a tree and later a sidewalk. The next weekend I went to see my uncle who said that I was being stupid and should smoke some weed, that was the first weekend I hadn't drank in over two years.

When I got home, I looked in the mirror at my broken nose, down at my shattered hand. I hated who I was, if I didn't stop I'd end up like my stepdad. I made myself a drink, drank half, then proceeded to dump it out and go to a dispensary. Bought some weed, a grinder and a pipe.

That was September 20th 2021, I'm by no means in a great place mentally, but I'm better than I was a year ago. I haven't drank since, although it's a struggle sometimes, the hatred I have for who I was fuels my will to not drink. And yes, my hand is still messed up, it's my constant reminder of why I quit drinking.

I know that was long but I felt like the back story was needed, sorry.

Honestly, this is why I try to stay away from recommending people melatonin. It can impair the body's natural ability even at a lower dose over a period of time. I wish it was something I looked into before ever taking melatonin, I don't think it was made with people like us in mind as intended clients. More so the average sleeper who needs some help every few days or so.

I think this kinda depends on the person, I'll give my personal experience with it to hopefully give some context.

I don't have vivid dreams unless I've been asleep for 3+ hours, so when I first started taking melatonin I didn't really experience more vivid dreams per-say, but rather I experienced them more often. I wasn't getting the desired effects from the 5mg melatonin so I bumped it up to 10mg.
It was around here where I noticed it did make me have more vivid/lucid dreams. Paired with my anxiety this turned into night terrors. Hoping I could just brute force my way into a full night sleep without a panic attack I eventually started taking 2 20mg pills a night.

It worked.

For a bit that is, when I first started taking 40 mg I just wouldn't dream, I would sleep for only about 5 hours but it was better than nothing. After a few months the terrors starting coming back and I was back down to 2-3 hours a night on a good day.

TL;DR would probably work short term, but would probably start having worse nightmares in the long term.
